title: ISO 13849-1:2023 — Safety of machinery: Safety-related parts of control systems — Part 1: General principles for design
ident: ISO 13849-1:2023 (4th edition); adopted as EN ISO 13849-1:2023
evidence: cencenelec.eu news page loaded live (CEN-CENELEC's own site): 'CEN Technical Committee 114 "Safety of machinery", just published an updated version of EN ISO 13849-1:2023 ... Safety of machinery - Safety-related parts of control systems - Part 1: General principles for design (ISO 13849-1:2023)', dated 2023-05-25. Cross-confirmed live via BSI (en-standard.eu): 'BS EN ISO 13849-1:2023 ... Released: 2023-05-04', 170 pp, ISBN 978 0 580 98533 1. ISO's own catalog title (iso.org/standard/73481.html) matches; direct iso.org fetch was blocked (403) but the CEN-CENELEC and BSI primary pages independently confirm the exact designation and date.

Completes the machinery-sector pairing with ISO 13849-1.

title: NPR 7150.2D — NASA Software Engineering Requirements
evidence: nodis3.gsfc.nasa.gov/displayDir.cfm?Internal_ID=N_PR_7150_002D_&page_name=Preface loaded live (NASA's own directive system): verbatim 'NPR 7150.2D / Effective Date: March 08, 2022 / Expiration Date: March 08, 2027' and 'Subject: NASA Software Engineering Requirements'.
note: The critic panel's exact finding: the corpus held the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook, 'Mars Code', and JPL's coding standard, but not the directive those rest on. Classifies software by safety criticality (Class A-E) and mandates the work products every NASA project must produce — the obligations-stage anchor for the whole US civil space programme, and now confirmed at its current (D) revision rather than the superseded A/B/C editions also indexed by NODIS.

evidence: cmu-sei.github.io (CMU Software Engineering Institute, redirected live from wiki.sei.cmu.edu) loaded live: 'ISO/IEC TS 17961:2013 ... WebSearch this session additionally surfaced iso.org's own catalog title (iso.org/standard/61134.html) and confirmed the TS was 'last reviewed and confirmed in 2024' (not withdrawn), plus a live MathWorks Polyspace Bug Finder documentation page (mathworks.com/help/bugfinder/ref/isoiects17961resident.html) implementing its rules — evidence this TS is applied to model-generated C via Polyspace, not only handwritten C.
